body:
It's clearer when in a separate block, and that prevents issues with sorting future headers added to the list.
I would also make the 3D server dependency explicit (currently I assume it's inherited from NavigationServer3D, which you'll also want to make opt out eventually).

Also personal taste nitpick, but for such short `#if` blocks (single line) and long condition name, with a single digit of difference between `PHYSICS_2D_DISABLED` and `PHYSICS_3D_DISABLED` which are often adjacent, having the condition repeated in the `#endif` as a comment actually hampers readability IMO. I won't die on that specific hill though, I also value consistency in applying that convention regardless of the number of lines in the block.

```suggestion
#include "servers/rendering_server.h"

#ifndef PHYSICS_2D_DISABLED
#include "servers/physics_server_2d.h"
#endif
#ifndef PHYSICS_3D_DISABLED
#include "servers/physics_server_3d.h"
#endif
```

That seems pretty weird.

I assume it's because of the dependency on Shape2D, but then I'd question whether Shape2D should really be disabled when disabling 2D physics.

It can be used for more than physics as seen here. It would also be used by #99911 for example, which, while they also have physics support, can be used for visual/spatial purposes only too.
Unused?

This is a pre-existing pattern here, but it's the only occurrence of `#ifdef PHYSICS_2D_DISABLED` instead of the double negative `#ifndef PHYSICS_2D_DISABLED`. It kind of makes sense as there's an `#else` but it throw me off a bit :P

Personally I'd expect to see the default/valid case handled first, so the double negative feels more natural. Very nitpicky yes :P

Same for the pre-existing 3D one.

```suggestion

#ifndef PHYSICS_3D_DISABLED
#include "scene/resources/3d/concave_polygon_shape_3d.h"
#endif // PHYSICS_3D_DISABLED

```
Move to its own block.

Move this block at the end, separate from the non-conditional includes.

We actually have as policy to use "absolute" includes for anything that's not the .h file matching the .cpp (with exceptions in modules and platform code which we want to keep self-contained, so their own headers are included with relative paths).

Keep the absolute path.

My issue with the advanced GUI PR isn't so much the diff noise but the `advanced` name, which feels quite arbitrary and doesn't make it easy to know where a given Control would be. While here if the folder is `physics` or `shapes`, once contributors understand that 2D shapes are there, it's easy to remember IMO.

But let's leave it like this for now and see if we want to refactor later.

Yeah let's leave it for future work. I suspect some of the 2D shapes or maybe viewport picking logic may be needed in some form even by some games which don't explicitly use 2D physics, but we'll found out if that happens.

This is opt-in so we're not breaking any game by default, so worst case is that some users who could benefit from this won't be able to use it just yet.
